prior_attempt.rejection: The first correction separated state borders from arrows, but treated stateArrowColor as unconditionally more specific than ArrowColor. Java normalizes both spellings to the same arrowColor style property, so their declarations override in source order.

second_rejection.rejection: The renderer's unified reverse alias lookup was correct for distinct parsed keys, but parse::collapse_reassigned_skinparams had already collapsed repeated raw spellings independently. It retained each raw key's first position, so a later repeated stateArrowColor could still sort before an intervening ArrowColor even though Java canonicalizes all family-arrow aliases before updating one map entry.

third_rejection.rejection: The parser compared ordinary declarations by the right cleaned identity but retained the first raw spelling, which downstream renderers cannot necessarily recognize after separator and family-arrow normalization. It also treated the appended synthetic theme tail as temporally later than every user declaration. PlantUML executes a theme synchronously where its directive occurs, so user skinparams after !theme must override theme values.

fourth_rejection.rejection: The parser retained the latest ordinary declaration's separator-normalized family spelling. A final UseCase.Arrow_Color therefore replaced the earlier arrow value under Java's correct shared identity but remained stored as usecasearrowcolor, which StateSkin could not see. Canonicalizing all records at the renderer would be wrong because flattened theme family entries intentionally remain distinct compatibility scopes.

implementations.change: Canonicalize every non-internal parsed skinparam before reassignment collapse.
implementations.evidence: The full no-oracle census fell from 11049/11251 to 11033/11251, entirely in preprocessing (264/307 to 248/307), while state remained 882/901.
implementations.finding: RustUML appends flattened entries from every theme family sub-block. Keys such as classArrowColor, stateArrowColor, and usecaseArrowColor in that synthetic body represent distinct style scopes selected later by each renderer; applying ordinary family-arrow replacement identity to those records destroys the compatibility model.

implementations.change: Store the fully cleaned ordinary replacement identity as every effective SkinParam.key while reconstructing theme order.
implementations.evidence: The parser suite remained green, but no-oracle fell from 11049/11251 to 11044/11251: sequenceMessageAlign lost four passes and sequenceParticipantPadding lost one.
implementations.finding: Replacement identity and downstream family spelling are separate concerns in RustUML's compatibility model. sequenceParticipantPadding and participantPadding compare through Java's cleaned identity, but existing renderers deliberately preserve their family spelling because their geometry differs. The effective record must carry the latest declaration's separator-normalized spelling while using the fully cleaned form only for replacement.

invariant: Java resolves state-image borders and state-diagram arrows from sibling style signatures. FromSkinparamToStyle maps stateBorderColor to root.element.stateDiagram.state LineColor. Before either its parameter map or style conversion sees an ordinary declaration, SkinParam.cleanForKeySlow lowercases and trims the key, removes underscores and dots, rewrites sequenceParticipant/sequenceActor aliases, rewrites every activity/class/component/object/sequence/state/usecase Arrow prefix to the shared arrow prefix, and rewrites a terminal align to alignment. SkinParam.setParam uses that cleaned key as replacement identity. RustUML's parsed SkinParam record also serves compatibility renderers that still consume family spellings, so its effective representation must retain the latest declaration's lowercased, separator-free spelling while comparing reassignments through the fully cleaned identity; retaining the first spelling loses the final declaration, while storing only the fully cleaned identity erases required family semantics. TContext.executeOneLineNotSafe dispatches a THEME line immediately to executeTheme, which reads the theme and calls executeLines before processing the next user line. Theme styles therefore occupy the directive's temporal position: user declarations before a theme can be superseded by it, and user declarations after it supersede matching theme properties. RustUML may continue relocating flattened theme output to preserve source-line numbers, but parser metadata must reconstruct this source order. Flattened theme family sub-blocks remain distinct scoped compatibility records and must not be merged by ordinary SkinParam family-arrow aliases. GraphvizImageBuilder and SvekEdge independently merge the selected arrow signature and derive the shaft and arrowhead Rainbow from it. The arrow signature may inherit the root or theme line color, but never the state sibling's explicit LineColor. A per-link color remains the final arrow-only override.
causal_divergence: Commit f55215d9 reconstructs theme execution order and compares ordinary declarations with the right cleanForKey identity, but stores every surviving ordinary declaration under only its latest separator-normalized spelling. That representation is necessary for compatibility keys whose family spelling still drives different Rust behavior, but it is incomplete for family-arrow aliases: Java erases the activity/class/component/object/sequence/state/usecase prefix before both map storage and style conversion, so an ordinary final UseCase.Arrow_Color is the shared arrowcolor declaration. Rust stores it as usecasearrowcolor. StateSkin recognizes statearrowcolor and arrowcolor, so inherited state arrows fall back to #181818 while a local transition override remains correct. Simply teaching StateSkin to accept every family spelling would make synthetic theme body entries leak across family scopes, undoing the no-oracle evidence that required those records to remain distinct.
planned_change: Keep the existing in-place theme marker/body reconstruction. Preserve separator-normalized family spellings for every synthetic theme-body record. For ordinary user-authored declarations only, continue comparing through the complete cleanForKey identity and retain only the last declaration at its effective source position; when that identity is arrowcolor, store it under the shared arrowcolor spelling because the family prefix has no surviving Java semantics. Continue retaining the latest separator-normalized spelling for compatibility identities such as participant padding and message alignment whose Rust consumers still distinguish families. Add parser tests proving all seven family-arrow aliases collapse to one ordinary arrowcolor record in source order while theme family-arrow records remain distinct, plus state-renderer coverage for a final cross-family alias and a local override. Preserve stateBorderColor isolation, theme ordering, per-transition precedence, and every prior heldout. Do not canonicalize arbitrary compatibility keys, merge theme family scopes, special-case fixture labels or colors, or alter SVG after emission.
